newsitem.title: GREECE: Balkan foreign ministers meet on regional problems.
newsitem.headline: Balkan foreign ministers meet on regional problems.

text.p: Balkan foreign ministers will strive to forge closer political and ecomomic ties and push for lasting peace in their turbulent region at a meeting in this northern Greek city starting on Monday.

"With this meeting we institutionalise for the first time, after an experimental meeting in Sofia, a forum where Balkan countries can gather and discuss Balkan problems," Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos told reporters.

Officials from Albania, Bulgaria, the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, Greece, Romania, Turkey and Serbia are expected to discuss trans-Balkan transport, energy and telecommunications projects, diplomats said.
They will also urge fair elections in Albania and discuss the implementation of the Dayton agreement in former Yugoslavia.

Albania, which has been gripped by violence since the collapse of pyramid investment schemes earlier this year, faces national elections on June 29. Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) observers are expected to monitor the poll.

The two-day meeting also aims to ease tensions in the multi-ethnic region, which peaked with the break-up of former Yugoslavia, by establishing co-operation in information networks and promoting cross-border business investment.
